records.people: Bo Bo Nge (deputy governor, Central Bank of Myanmar)
records.summary: Bo Bo Nge, the deputy governor of Myanmar's Central Bank, was arrested at his home on the day of the 1 February 2021 military takeover and in May 2022 was charged by the Anti-Corruption Commission over matters including failing to tax donations and failing to monitor foreign exchange management. In December 2022 a junta court sentenced him to 20 years in prison for graft after a months-long secret trial, over what it said was mismanagement of banks trading foreign currency. His former adviser Sean Turnell called the sentencing hypocritical and said the jailed people were the reformers while corrupt bankers remained free.
records.source_title: Myanmar junta sentences former Central Bank official to 20 years in prison (Radio Free Asia)

searched_none.note: Checked 15 Nov 2026: no Public Accounts Committee report on the National Investment Fund published or tabled yet. Searched Bahamian Parliament, tribune242, EyeWitness News and Nassau Guardian; latest confirmed item remains governor John Rolle's Sept 2026 letters confirming the NIF board was never formally convened and that the Central Bank maintains an account named 'National Investment Fund' with transactions from July 2025. No PAC finding to cite.
National Audit Office annual reports (incl. 2024 report, 3 May 2025) and Arabic searches of ديوان الرقابة المالية والإدارية: no finding naming the Central Bank of Bahrain.
Auditor General of Bermuda reports, Royal Gazette and bernews: only BMA enforcement actions and a civil suit against the BMA; no case with the BMA as subject.
Brunei Anti-Corruption Bureau prosecutions via thescoop and The Star: cases involve courts, immigration, customs, police, tourism; none at BDCB/AMBD.
Office of the Auditor General and news searches: only a commercial-bank (RBC) employee case; nothing with the Bank of Canada as subject.
Tribunal de Contas, Procuradoria-Geral and Supremo Tribunal de Justiça case summaries: no case or audit finding naming Banco de Cabo Verde.
Closed vein per brief (BCD publishes its own unqualified external audits). Searched French-language court/prosecutor coverage instead: nothing found.
Rigsrevisionen and Statsrevisorerne reports, Danish-language searches: no finding or case involving Danmarks Nationalbank.
Central Auditing Organization reports via parlmany, Administrative Prosecution referrals and Arabic court coverage: hits concern other bodies, or the CBE acting as regulator (e.g. CIB probe).
Only diaspora opinion sites discuss the Bank of Eritrea; no official, court or major-outlet source.
Closed vein per brief (Auditor General does not cover the RBF). Tried FICAC press releases and PacLII instead; the Reserve Bank hit was in fact a military finance officer case.
One record filed (Bo Bo Nge). No further distinct case found.
State Audit Institution (sai.gov.om) annual reports and Omani press: corruption cases concern ministries and commercial banks, not the Central Bank of Oman.

State Audit and Administrative Control Bureau, Anti-Corruption Commission and AMAN's 2025 study on corruption-risk management at the Palestine Monetary Authority: the study is a risk assessment with no documented episode, names or amounts.
Diwan Al Muhasaba (State Audit Bureau) coverage in Arabic: referrals named medical centres and a ministry unit; nothing on Qatar Central Bank.
Nazaha monthly bulletins and Arabic searches: detainees listed are from other government bodies or commercial banks; nothing naming the Saudi Central Bank.

Empowerment Removal/Anti-Corruption Committee material checked: it dissolved the Central Bank board in Feb 2020 over alleged links to the ousted regime and in Aug 2021 reported fraud in 90 bank accounts without naming the Central Bank; the Oct 2025 dabanga piece on conflicts of interest records only dismissals of the governor and a deputy, with no finding against anyone. Treated as moves against the bank or characterisation, not corruption cases.
Auditor-General's Office reports and parliamentary material: every MAS item found is MAS enforcing against financial institutions.

Corte de Cuentas and court coverage: the one hit, ex-BCR president Carlos Federico Paredes, was an estafa conviction over 2006-2008 private land sales later time-barred by the Sala de lo Penal; no central bank money involved, so it fails the subject test.

Accounts Chamber, prosecutor bulletins and the Central Bank's own 2025 annual report (compliance and internal audit sections, read in full): only prevention measures, no staff disciplinary or fraud episode. Embezzlement cases found are all at commercial/state banks.
Closed vein per brief (no FY2021 management-letter issues). Tried Samoa Supreme Court judgments instead; the Central Bank hit (Telea Laupapa) was theft at the Land Transport Authority, not the bank.
